brief.t: As of 2026-10-16, old-crop (2026/27) unfixed call **sales** are 68.2k contracts (+155 w/w, -3,167 over 8 weeks) and old-crop unfixed **purchases** 29.8k (-94 w/w). Against the same week of the last five seasons, sales are at the 40th percentile (avg 78.4k) and purchases at the 40th (avg 39.8k). Beyond this season, merchants hold 11.2k of new-crop sales and 35.0k of new-crop purchases.

Net old-crop on-call is +38,397 (mill side). In old-crop COT, producers/merchants/processors/users hold 99.6k long and 231.8k short (net -132,247, +3,410 w/w). Their long/short ratio of 0.43 sits at the 19th percentile of the last three years: **commercials hold relatively little long cover, so fixing the mill-side book is more likely to need buying in the market**. The net and the ratio matter more than gross longs, which include calendar-spread legs held by trade houses. On the other side, total unfixed purchases of 64.8k (-2,899 over 8 weeks) compare with 253.2k PMU shorts and 31.1k swap-dealer shorts — producer fixing is latent selling, whether it runs through PMU hedges or swap structures.

Front contract **December 2026** is 5.6 weeks from first notice, with 17.1k unfixed sales and 19.7k unfixed purchases against 166.7k open interest. Next: March 2027 with 24.0k unfixed sales. The Dec/Mar spread is -3.72¢, -0.48¢ on the week.

Old-crop unfixed sales of 7.11m bales equal 16% of USDA's 2026/27 world trade forecast (44.7m, October 2026). USDA sees Brazil exporting 16.0m bales vs the US 12.3m. US export sales (week of 2026-10-15): 4.16m running bales unshipped, China 6%.

Managed money is net long 66.5k (+767 w/w; 3-yr COT index 78). Spec length is elevated; with commercials light on long cover, mill fixing could still add buying, but a long spec book can also liquidate.
